citationText: 24. Dr. Zworykin and Gregory Ogloblinsky were having poor results with the crude two-sided camera tubes they were building. See V. K. Zworykin and George A. Morton, Television — the Electronics of Image Transmission , p. 304, John Wiley & Sons, Inc.: New York, 1940. It is known that Zworykin had Dr. Wilson of Westinghouse build several dissector tubes after his visit to the Green Street Labs in April 1930, based on Farnsworth's design, and was using them quite successfully — so successfully, in fact, that this was the main reason for Sarnoff's visit to the Green Street Labs in May 1931. This is from U.S. Pat. Interference #64,027.
